newsitem.title: USA: Outer Banks evacuates one island ahead of Fran.
newsitem.headline: Outer Banks evacuates one island ahead of Fran.

text.p: Emergency management officials worried about the dangerous strength of Hurricane Fran began evacuating residents of this low-lying resort island late Wednesday.

Peter Stone, emergency management manager for the tiny island that is part of North Carolina's famed Outer Banks, said the decision was based on the proximity of storm and the forecast for it to grow stronger.
"It was time to get everybody the hell out of here," Stone said, referring to the 5 p.m. EDT evacuation order.

Fran was packing winds of 115 mph (185 km) and was expected to strike the South Carolina coast late Thursday, according to the National Hurricane Center. Forecasters remained concerned that conditions were ripe for Fran's winds to grow even stronger before making landfall.
And a small wobble detected in the path of the eye of the storm could push its landfall away from the Charleston, S.C. area and toward the Outer Banks of North Carolina, local officials said.

Ocracoke Island, a sliver of flood-prone land near Cape Hatteras, has about 800 permanent residents and an estimated 2,000 tourists. Three ferries and a two-lane highway are the only ways to get on and off the island.
In nearby Dare County, emergency management officials said they planned to meet after 11 p.m. EDT to discuss a possible evacuation.

"It's very similar to the Hurricane Edouard situation last week," said Clarence Skinner, head of the Dare County emergency management group. "Time is our big problem... If Fran did turn, we'd have to take action early in the morning, probably by 8 a.m. EDT, to get people out of here."
